scenarios: the opened pull request's receipt is COMPENSATABLE; UndoToolCall refuses it NOT_UNDOABLE naming forge.pr.update
CompensateEffect asks for its own approval first (nothing reaches the forge), then closes the pull request once
the compensation receipt is a new effect naming the original (compensates), IRREVERSIBLE itself, beside the untouched original; the chain verifies
a second request answers from the compensation receipt; the compensation can be neither undone nor compensated
after a kill and restart the chain with the new fields verifies from the projection and reads back identical
a pre-V17 receipt keeps its hash; relabelling a compensatable effect as reversible breaks the chain

ci.note: every Rust job green on macOS, Linux and Windows; the macOS desktop-E2E job passed on rerun after a states.spec restart-window render race unrelated to receipts (it passed on Linux and Windows in the same run)

audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: effect classes and a hash-chained receipt existed, but no receipt said how far its effect could be taken back, UndoToolCall answered NOTHING_TO_UNDO ('the call changed no files') for an opened pull request, and there was no compensation path or compensation receipt.
proof: Real Core against a GitHub-compatible forge and a real bare remote: an external effect is labelled COMPENSATABLE and refused an undo; its compensation runs under approval once and leaves a distinct receipt linked to the original; the chain verifies across a restart.
negative_proof: The receipt chain rejects a relabelled class; the compensation itself is refused both undo and compensation.
limitations: One declared compensation (forge.pr.create -> close); MCP and browser effects are IRREVERSIBLE until their tools declare one; PARTIALLY_REVERSIBLE effects keep the typed content undo.
